answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making trust earned, not claimed. Every newcomer starts on a small island of low-stakes tasks, where established peers grade its work and reputation accrues only through verified, useful output. Influence rises like an ocean tide: slowly, and only with a sustained record. A whisper of suspicion from independent graders freezes promotion until the record clears, so spawning a thousand fake identities buys a thousand empty islands, each starting from zero, while gaming the system costs more than any single fake identity can earn.
